Undivided-interest diligence (Kensington: Kensington Gardens is undivided-interest ownership, so there's no Form B, depreciation report or reserve fund; check the ownership agreement and title instead.
The Halifax Street condo buildings the s: The Halifax Street condo buildings that come up in searches (Marquis Grande at 4132 Halifax, and Brent Gardens or Brentwood Gardens at 4363 and 4373 Halifax) are listed under Brentwood Park, with Parkcrest mentioned only as nearby.

Tenure is not uniform across the city: a: Ownership isn't the same across the city: at UniverCity on Burnaby Mountain, homes are leasehold, prepaid on 99-year ground leases from the SFU Community Trust, and one listing says its lease runs to 2109. Don't assume freehold on the mountain.
Check tenure before anything else on Bur: On Burnaby Mountain, check ownership first: UniverCity land is leasehold, on prepaid 99-year SFU Community Trust ground leases, so the title search, not the listing, shows what you'd actually own.
UniverCity product sits on leasehold pre: UniverCity homes are leasehold, on prepaid 99-year SFU Community Trust ground leases, and one listing's lease runs to 2109. Read the lease and its expiry before comparing a mountain property's value with a fee-simple lot elsewhere in Burnaby.

The strata budget rule to check on a For: On the Form B, check the contingency reserve fund: since November 1, 2023, a strata must put at least 10% of its annual operating budget into it when it approves the budget.
A wood-frame low-rise; the majority of l: A wood-frame low-rise; most listings say it was built in 1975 (one says 1976). The building directory's Terramor page r: A building directory lists Terramor at 9088 Halston Court as built in 2006 with 177 units, pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed, plus a clubhouse, gym, in-suite laundry, outdoor pool, sauna and hot tub. Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the strata homes are: I don't know of any condo buildings in the area. The named strata stock is the Greentree: The strata homes are the Greentree Village townhouses, in several phases with the same name; the homes around them are detached houses. The board's "condos and townhomes" figure for the area combines both.
Townhouse-form stock in Metrotown is mos: Townhouses in Metrotown come in two forms: street-facing townhouses at the base of towers (City applications on Wilson Avenue and Telford Avenue include them), and ground-level units on the residential streets west of the station.

A strata high-rise at the Halifax / Phil: The Ambassador, a concrete strata high-rise at Halifax and Phillips: listings show condos built in 1987, with strata fees. A full MLS report for a unit in the comp: Montecito 2000: an MLS report for a unit gives plan NWS90 with 75 units, freehold strata townhouses managed by Strataco, with an outdoor pool and clubhouse. A building directory says pets and rentals are allowed with restrictions; confirm on the Form B.

Tenure — this area's defining fact: ever: Ownership is the key fact here: every market home in UniverCity is leasehold strata, prepaid on a 99-year ground lease from the SFU Community Trust. SFU keeps the land and the Trust leases serviced lots to developers for 99 years, so the homes are leasehold, not freehold. Listings show this as "Leasehold prepaid-Strata", and one says its building's lease runs to 2109.
The area is the top of Burnaby Mountain: The area is the top of Burnaby Mountain: Simon Fraser University's Burnaby campus and the UniverCity community beside it. The real estate board calls it "Simon Fraser University"; "Simon Fraser Hills", on the Forest Grove side, is a separate area.
Where the condo stock concentrates: in U: Where the condos are: in UniverCity's four neighbourhoods (West Highlands, East Highlands, High Street and the Slopes), around University High Street, University Crescent and Tower Road, south and east of campus. The plan allows up to 4,536 homes for up to 10,000 residents on about 65 hectares at build-out.
Plan and zoning frame: the Burnaby 2050: Plans and zoning: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 plan) covers the whole city, and UniverCity has its own plan dating from its 1996 approvals. Zoning is Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815, adopted June 9, 2026, in effect July 1, 2026), which replaced the 1965 bylaw.
Schools (SD41): University Highlands Ele: Schools (SD41 Burnaby): University Highlands Elementary is inside UniverCity (LEED Gold; the school says most families can walk there in under 5 minutes), and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8800 Eastlake Drive) is the public secondary school on the mountain. The School Locator puts the secondary's own address in the Cameron Elementary (K–7) and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12) catchments, while Slopes Mews listings name University Highlands and Burnaby Mountain. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Form B diligence (leasehold strata): a U: A UniverCity strata is still a strata corporation, so read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. The Form B doesn't cover the ground lease, so read both.
Named buildings verified in the local in: Buildings include Altitude (9060 and 9080 University Crescent), Origin (9150 University High Street), The Nest by Mosaic (9250 University High Street), The Hub by Liberty Homes (9009 Cornerstone Mews) and Centre Block (9393 Tower Road); confirm the address on title for a specific unit.
Both, in that order of risk: the Form B: Both, the lease first: the Form B for the strata's finances and bylaws, and the ground lease for its start date, remaining term, prepaid status and what happens at the end of the term. Lenders and lawyers look hardest at the lease, and some lenders limit mortgage terms based on how much of the lease is left.
Simon Fraser University is the top of Bu: Simon Fraser University is the top of Burnaby Mountain: SFU's Burnaby campus and the UniverCity community beside it. It's also the real estate board's name for the area. "Simon Fraser Hills", on the Forest Grove side of the mountain, is a separate area.
Schools (SD41): University Highlands Ele: Schools (SD41 Burnaby): University Highlands Elementary is inside UniverCity (LEED Gold; the school says most families can walk there in under 5 minutes), and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8800 Eastlake Drive) is the public secondary school on the mountain. The School Locator puts the secondary's own address in the Cameron Elementary (K–7) and Burnaby Mountain Secondary (8–12) catchments. Strata frame (the form every UniverCity: Strata rules: every UniverCity purchase is a strata purchase, so read the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the depreciation report; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page) alongside the ground lease, which the Form B doesn't cover. Landmarks: Deer Lake Park (main address: Landmarks: Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Avenue, reached from Sperling Avenue), with the Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant; Burnaby Lake Regional Park, around the lake just north of Lougheed Highway; and Bill Copeland Sports Centre (3676 Kensington Avenue) at the Burnaby Lake Sports Complex on the northwest edge. Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: there aren't really any. The area is almost all detached houses (modest post-war bungalows on the flatter western streets, and large custom homes in Buckingham Heights), mostly freehold. Anchors and edges: Deer Lake Park (6450: Landmarks: Deer Lake Park (6450 Deer Lake Avenue, reached from Sperling Avenue), with the Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House; Burnaby City Hall (4949 Canada Way) just west; and Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street) just south of Canada Way, which is being redeveloped in phases (Phase 1, a six-storey, 83-bed pavilion, 2021–2026; Phase 2 dates not yet set). Not in this sub-area: The Duthie Avenue: Not necessarily in this area: a property on Duthie Avenue shares the area's name but may be listed in a neighbouring area; check the listing's area.

Where the condo stock concentrates: ther: Where the strata homes are: there are very few, and the ones I know of are townhouses, not apartments, in one group on Cumberland Street and Cumberland Place on the north side (Deerfield, Wildflower and Chancery Lane).
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: in one group of three complexes on Cumberland Street and Cumberland Place on the north side, near Burnaby Lake and the greenbelt (Deerfield, Wildflower and Chancery Lane). The rest of the area is mostly detached houses on East Burnaby side streets.
SnapStats publishes medians at community: There are no medians for The Crest itself. For all of Burnaby in September 2026, the detached median was $1,825,000 ($662 per sq ft, 96% of list price, 37 days on the market), and the condo and townhome median $686,000 ($763 per sq ft, 98%, 36 days); that's condos and townhomes combined, not a townhome figure.
SSMUH / suite rules as the City states t: Small-scale housing and suites: in June 2024, Burnaby combined its single- and two-family zones into one R1 zone that allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, with a minimum lot of 10 m wide and 281 m². The zone allows houses, duplexes, multiplexes, rowhouses and secondary suites, and lots with two or more main units can be stratified, which is where future townhouse-style homes on Crest house lots could come from.
Vancouver Heights is a City of Burnaby n: Vancouver Heights is a North Burnaby neighbourhood on and below the Capitol Hill rise, with Hastings Street as its main street; it's also the real estate board's name for the area. It runs roughly from Boundary Road west to Gamma Avenue east, and from Hastings Street north to Burrard Inlet. West of Boundary Road is the City of Vancouver (Hastings-Sunrise), a different city and area.
Where condo stock concentrates: low-rise: Where the condos are: low-rise strata buildings on Hastings Street and one block north on Albert Street. The rest of the area is mostly detached houses on a sloping hillside with views: early-to-mid-1900s homes, post-war bungalows and Vancouver Specials alongside newer rebuilds.
Schools and catchments (SD41, Burnaby):: Schools (SD41 Burnaby): two elementary schools are on Pandora Street in the area, Confederation Park Elementary (4715 Pandora Street) and Rosser Elementary (4375 Pandora Street), and the catchment splits the street by address: 4375 Pandora is in Rosser Elementary and Alpha Secondary, and 4715 Pandora is in Confederation Park Elementary and Alpha Secondary. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Schools (SD41) — settled chain cited: th: Schools (SD41 Burnaby): Rosser Elementary (K–7), 4375 Pandora Street, and Confederation Park Elementary (K–7), 4715 Pandora Street, both in the area, with Alpha Secondary (8–12) as the secondary. The two elementaries split Pandora Street by address (4303–4375 Pandora is in Rosser's catchment), while both are in Alpha's. Burnaby North Secondary (751 Hammarskjold Drive) is the other North Burnaby secondary, but being nearby doesn't put you in its catchment. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Form B diligence (strata frame): Strata: For any strata purchase, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
On and just off Hastings Street: four co: On and just off Hastings Street: The Sienna (3939 Hastings Street, 1998, 22 units), The Carleton (4223 Hastings Street, 2020, 22 units), Heritage Green (3978 Albert Street, 1994, 28 units) and Evergreen Place (3861 Albert Street, 1989), plus The Mondeo (3811 Hastings Street), Verdi (3971 Hastings Street) and Carleton Terrace (4160 Albert Street).
Alpha Secondary, on the settled SD41 loc: Alpha Secondary: the School Locator puts both 4375 and 4715 Pandora Street in Alpha's catchment. Burnaby North Secondary is also in North Burnaby, but it isn't the catchment secondary for those Pandora addresses.
The sub-area's stock is detached houses: Homes here are detached houses on fee-simple lots, typical Burnaby lots with larger, steeper view lots on the hill; Capitol Hill's upper streets are known for views over Burrard Inlet, downtown Vancouver and the North Shore mountains. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees; the title, Burnaby bylaws and any registered covenants apply.
Over October 2025 – September 2026 the B: From October 2025 to September 2026, Burnaby's detached median ranged from $1,750,000 (June 2026) to $1,992,500 (December 2025), and the condo and townhome median from $643,250 (July 2026) to $720,000 (October 2025).
Housing fabric: predominantly detached s: Homes: mostly detached houses on a sloping hillside with views, from early-to-mid-1900s homes, post-war bungalows and Vancouver Specials to newer custom rebuilds, with a few low-rise condos along Hastings Street. Most homes are freehold; the strata homes are on or near Hastings.
Schools (SD41 Burnaby): two SD41 element: Schools (SD41 Burnaby): two elementary schools are on Pandora Street in the area, Confederation Park Elementary (K–7), 4715 Pandora Street, and Rosser Elementary (K–7), 4375 Pandora Street. They split the street by address (4303–4375 Pandora is in Rosser's catchment, 4715 Pandora in Confederation Park's), and both addresses are in the Alpha Secondary catchment. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
The civic cluster is mid-replacement — a: The community centre is due to be replaced, but the project is on hold. The new Confederation Park Community Centre would keep the McGill library branch (built 2001) and Eileen Dailly pool (built 1992) and replace the 1971 seniors centre, but the City says the project has been deferred, so the 1971 centre is still the one in use.
The usual duplex form: The housing stock: The usual duplex form: the area is mostly detached houses on a sloping hillside with views, mostly freehold, on typical Burnaby lots with larger, steeper view lots on the hill. A duplex here would be two units built on one of those lots and stratified, which the current zoning allows.
Transit: Routes 131 Hastings at Gilmore: Transit: routes 131 (Hastings at Gilmore / Kootenay Loop) and 132 (Capitol Hill / Hastings at Gilmore) run along Albert Street past the building from the MacDonald at Albert stop, and the 131 continues to Kootenay Loop. The R5 Hastings Street RapidBus runs one block south, from Burrard Station to SFU, at least every 10 minutes at peak times and every 15 minutes otherwise.
Transit: R5 Hastings Street RapidBus, Tr: Transit: the R5 Hastings Street RapidBus runs along Hastings from Burrard Station downtown to SFU, at least every 10 minutes at peak times and every 15 minutes otherwise. The R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus runs from Park Royal to Metrotown Station, serving the Heights at Willingdon Avenue every 6 to 7 minutes at weekday peak times and every 10 to 15 minutes otherwise. Kootenay Loop, the bus exchange at the end of route 131, is to the west along Hastings.

Transit: the R5 Hastings Street RapidBus stops on Hastings by the building, running from Burrard Station to SFU at least every 10 minutes at peak times and every 15 minutes otherwise. Routes 131 (Hastings at Gilmore / Kootenay Loop) and 132 (Capitol Hill / Hastings at Gilmore) stop at Hastings and Gilmore by the building, and the 131 continues via Gilmore, Albert and MacDonald to Kootenay Loop.
Official City sources show detached hous: City sources show detached houses around the park and no named condo building. Apple Greene is on this page because listings at 8720–8880 No. 1 Road put it in the real estate board's "Boyd Park" area; City planning documents don't use that name for it.
Form B diligence (Apple Greene — the poc: For Apple Greene, the area's one strata complex (apartments), read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Directory pet and rental lines aren't the bylaws; the Form B and registered bylaws are. There's no townhouse strata here today.
Fee-simple homes (the pocket's detached: Fee-simple homes: I don't know of any fee-simple townhouse complex here; the fee-simple homes are detached houses, some with suite potential (see below).
Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500, Official Com: Zoning and plans: Richmond Zoning Bylaw 8500, the Richmond 2041 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 9000) and the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 apply. The plan has no Boyd Park area plan; the land around it is planned as Seafair / West Richmond. Houses around the park are zoned Single Detached (RS1 and RS2), with minimum lot areas that vary by subzone (RS1/B 360 m², RS1/E 550 m², RS1/F 828 m² and RS1/K 315 m²) and a 24 m minimum depth in most subzones; the small-scale multi-unit zones (RSM/S, RSM/M, RSM/L and RSM/XL) also apply. Check the zone and dimensions of a specific lot with the City.
OCP — City of Richmond 2041 Official Com: Official Community Plan: the Richmond 2041 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 9000) covers the area, with area plans for neighbourhood issues; there's no Boyd Park area plan, and the land around it is planned as Seafair / West Richmond.
By Dava Developments, per current listin: Built by Dava Developments, according to listings, which describe a riverfront master-planned community with about 5 acres of parkland and dike trails. Strata plan EPS4428, built in 2018, wood frame, with geothermal heating and cooling, air conditioning, a gym and recreation facilities. A building directory says pets are allowed. Sources differ on size: one listing describes a 98-unit development at this address, while a unit's property page says it's one of 35 units at 10177 River Drive; one figure may be for a single phase.
Where the condo stock concentrates: one: Where the condos are: along River Drive, running west from the No. 3 Road side along the North Arm dike, where Dava Developments built the Parc Riviera riverfront community (apartments at 10033 and 10177 River Drive, townhouses at 10333 River Drive). The City Centre Area Plan describes the village core itself as an industrial area in transition, with lots of different sizes, an incomplete street grid and old rail lines. Away from River Drive, the nearest homes are on Bridgeport Road to the south: detached houses and a townhouse rezoning at 10760 and 10780 Bridgeport Road and 3033, 3091 and 3111 Shell Road.
A townhouse complex at the west end of R: A townhouse complex at the west end of River Drive, built in 2020 with 86 units according to a building directory (one listing says 2021). Listings show row townhouses with strata fees, and the directory says pets and rentals are allowed with restrictions; confirm on the Form B. Listings mention a clubhouse, with a daycare and playground in the master plan.
Stacked townhomes in the Parc Riviera co: Stacked townhomes in the Parc Riviera community: the presale source describes 80 townhomes in eleven four-storey and four three-storey wood-frame buildings linked by a skywalk, and a listing shows freehold strata townhouses built in 2025, with heat-pump heating and air conditioning. A listing says other floor plans are still available from the developer, so some units may be developer sales, where GST and the presale rules apply. Check rental and pet rules on the Form B.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: along River Drive, west along the North Arm dike, in the Parc Riviera master plan (Parc Riviera Mews, Northview Estates and Parc Portofino), and on Bridgeport Road south of the village (North Gate Residences at Shell Road). The City Centre Area Plan describes the village core itself as an industrial area in transition, with lots of different sizes, an incomplete street grid and old rail lines.
Form B diligence (all 4 strata complexes: For each of the four strata complexes, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Directory rental and pet lines aren't the bylaws. The River Drive listings mention geothermal heating and cooling, and at the Parc Riviera apartments, water and sewer included in the strata fee, so check what each strata's fee covers before comparing fees.
Serviced position, as official sources s: Services: homes in Richmond are on City water and sewer. Check servicing for a specific lot with the City.
Zoning — Zoning Bylaw 8500: Richmond lan: Zoning: Richmond's Zoning Bylaw 8500 applies, and in Bridgeport Village the City Centre Area Plan sets land use. The Urban Centre T5 areas allow office, hotel, institutional, studio, retail and entertainment uses but no homes, and the General Urban T4 areas with an Industrial Reserve overlay allow light industry but no homes. The houses on the Bridgeport Road corridor are zoned RS1/F, with the townhouse (RTM3) rezoning above. Check a property's zone and area plan designation before pricing any use.
Airport overlays — diligence items: the: Airport rules: the Aircraft Noise Sensitive Development Policy applies throughout Bridgeport Village, and City data sheets put sites in Aircraft Noise Sensitive Use Areas 1B and 2. Bridgeport Station is a provincial Transit-Oriented Area, but federal airport zoning height limits take priority over its heights here.
Schools: Robert J Tait Elementary, grade: Schools (SD38 Richmond): Robert J. Tait Elementary (K–7), 10071 Finlayson Drive; R. C. Talmey Elementary (K–7), 9500 Kilby Drive; and Cambie Secondary (8–12), 4151 Jacombs Road. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there are no apartment condos. The area is mostly detached houses; the Area Plan expected townhouses or apartments along some major roads, and the strata homes that were built are townhouses on and near Cambie Road and No. 5 Road.
Richmond zoning and plans: the area's ba: Zoning and plans: the area is mostly zoned Single Detached (RS1/RS2) under Zoning Bylaw 8500. The RS1/E subzone on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot of 550 m², 18 m wide and 24 m deep, with one house per lot and a secondary suite allowed. The East Cambie Area Plan (adopted October 21, 2002, land use map updated by Bylaw 9874) sits under the Richmond 2041 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 9000), and the City started updating the plan toward 2050 in fall 2024. In East Cambie, multi-family sites need a development permit.
Flood rules — the Richmond-specific dili: Flooding: all of Richmond is designated floodplain under Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204, which sets flood construction levels that living space must meet unless an exemption applies. Richmond averages 1 metre above sea level, behind 49 km of dikes designed for a 1-in-500-year flood, with dikes being raised from 3.5 to 4.7 metres, and the Area Plan requires new East Cambie development to provide adequate flood protection. Check the strata insurance and flood level compliance for a specific building.
Current listings describe townhouse unit: Listings show townhouses at the Normandie, one saying pets are allowed and describing a 77-unit wood-frame development (from a building directory); another refers to the strata plan for the unit. Check other rules on the Form B.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: on Cambie Road west of No. 5 Road (Cambie Gardens and Cambie Court); in the McNeely Drive and Jack Bell Drive pocket south of Cambie Road (Sausalito, Francisco Village, Capistrano and Malibu, plus Normandie on Thorpe Road); and at No. 5 Road and Highway 91 (Wembley). Otherwise the area is mostly detached houses; the Area Plan expected townhouses or apartments along some major roads.

Lot character from the zone: the RS1/E s: Lot sizes: the RS1/E subzone on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot of 550 m², 18 m wide and 24 m deep under Zoning Bylaw 8500, with one house per lot and a secondary suite allowed. Those are the zone's minimums, not actual lot sizes; other subzones apply elsewhere in the area, so check a specific lot with the City.
Civic anchors: King George / Cambie Comm: Nearby: King George / Cambie Community Park, 4100 No. 5 Road (heritage trees, basketball and tennis courts, playgrounds, a water park and picnic areas; the area's main park); Richmond Nature Park, 11851 Westminster Highway (over 100 acres of old bog forest, in the ALR); Cambie Community Centre, 12800 Cambie Road; the Cambie library branch, 150-11590 Cambie Road; Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway; and the Richmond East Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 95-10551 Shellbridge Way.
The usual duplex form: The area's base z: The usual duplex form: the area is mostly zoned Single Detached (RS1/RS2), and the RS1/E subzone on Cambie Road sets a minimum lot of 550 m², 18 m wide and 24 m deep, with one main house. East Cambie's duplexes are individual duplex buildings on single lots, built under the zoning of their day, with the province's small-scale housing rules now applying. Check a specific duplex's title (one lot, a strata plan, or two subdivided lots).
North Arm is the GVR board sub-area name: North Arm is the real estate board's name for the New Westminster area along the North Arm of the Fraser River: the riverfront on the south side of mainland New Westminster, below the Marine Way and Stewardson Way corridor, with the Waterfront Esplanade (North Arm) trail along the river.
The Queensborough Bridge is the sub-area: The Queensborough Bridge is the area's link: it carries Highway 91A over the North Arm between the mainland and Queensborough, which is why Queensborough addresses like Mercer Village, Port Royal and Portside come up in "North Arm" searches, even though Queensborough is a separate area across the water.
Slope house parcels: houses on the slope: House lots on the slope: houses above the riverfront are in the Single Detached Residential zones (RS) of Zoning Bylaw 6680, 2001; the RS-1 zone requires a lot of at least 557.4 m² (6,000 sq ft) and a floor space ratio of no more than 0.5.
Civic anchors: the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic a: Nearby: the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue (fully opened in May 2024; 10,644 m², the City's largest project to date), is the city's main recreation centre, up the hill from the river. The main New Westminster library is at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown, with a kiosk and holds locker at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, downtown, and the city's hospital is Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, in Sapperton.
Where the condo stock concentrates: it d: Where the condos are: there aren't any. The area is detached houses in the Single Detached (RS1/RS2) zones, and I don't know of any condo building or townhouse complex here. The nearest transit hub is outside the area: Richmond-Brighouse Station on the Canada Line, on No. 3 Road to the east, which the City has identified as a Transit-Oriented Area.
Local anchors: Quilchena Elementary Scho: Nearby: Quilchena Elementary, 3760 Moresby Drive; Thompson Community Centre, 5151 Granville Avenue, north across Granville; the Brighouse (main) library branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate, in the City Centre; and Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway.
Form B diligence (strata purchases gener: For a strata purchase, including later resales at Quilchena West, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Buying a presale works from the developer's disclosure statement instead (see the presale rules below).
Richmond zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw: Zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw 8500 applies, and most of the area is zoned Single Detached (RS1/RS2), with minimum lot areas by subzone including 360 m² (RS1/B and RS2/B), 550 m² (RS1/E), 828 m² (RS1/F) and 2,000 m² (RS1/G), and a secondary suite allowed. The city-wide plan is Richmond's 2041 Official Community Plan (Bylaw 9000), and the Laurelwood Sub-Area Plan covers the bend at Granville Avenue and Railway Avenue.
Main roads: Granville Avenue and Railway: Main roads and transit: Granville Avenue and Railway Avenue are the main roads at this bend. The nearest Canada Line station is Richmond-Brighouse on No. 3 Road, to the east, a Transit-Oriented Area. Route 401 (One Road) runs from Richmond-Brighouse Station via No. 3 Road, Westminster Highway and No. 1 Road to Steveston.
Civic anchors: Thompson Community Centre: Nearby: Thompson Community Centre, 5151 Granville Avenue, north across Granville; the Brighouse (main) library branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate, in the City Centre; Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway; and the Richmond City Centre Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 110-4671 No. 3 Road.
Geography note: \"Riverdale\" is not a C: "Riverdale" isn't a City of Richmond planning name; the City plans and serves this area as part of Thompson, and "Riverdale" is the real estate board's name for it. It's the Riverdale Drive pocket in northwest Richmond, west of No. 2 Road and south of Westminster Highway, running south toward Granville Avenue; the City places McCallan Neighbourhood Park "West of No. 2 Road and South of Westminster Hwy., off Riverdale Drive and Larkspur Avenue" in the Thompson area. There's no official boundary for a Riverdale neighbourhood.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowh: Where the condos are: there aren't any. The area is detached houses on large lots, zoned RS1/RS2 under Zoning Bylaw 8500 (subzone minimums range from 360 m² for RS1/B to 2,000 m² for RS1/G).
Suites and added units: a secondary suit: Suites and extra units: a secondary suite is allowed in the RS1/RS2 zones, from 33 m² up to 40% of the house's floor area or 110 m², whichever is less. The City allows at least one secondary suite or extra unit such as a coach house per lot, and the provincial small-scale housing rules allow at least 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on larger lots. For most buyers here, that's where extra homes come from, not condos.
Lot character from the zone ladder, as s: Lot sizes: RS1/RS2 minimum lot areas vary widely by subzone (RS1/B 360 m², RS1/E 550 m², RS1/F 828 m², RS1/K 315 m² and RS1/G 2,000 m²), with a 24 m minimum depth in most subzones. Those are the zone's minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot with the City.
Historic subdivision fabric = built lot: The streets are an established detached subdivision, not land for sale, and I don't know of any land assembly, development site, rezoning or major project planned for the area.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates:: Where the townhouses are: on the south edge, on Williams Road (Edgewater Park) and Francis Road (Seafair West), the area's two townhouse complexes. Otherwise the area is almost all detached houses; the one apartment building I know of is a rental building.
District energy (ADEU) — not a Seafair c: District energy charges don't apply here: the Alexandra District Energy Utility serves only the West Cambie / Alexandra neighbourhood (Bylaw 8641 covers buildings there). As far as I know, Seafair isn't in its service area, and no Seafair complex pays its rates.
No market figures are stated for this ar: There are no market figures here for Steveston North: the monthly market report I use doesn't cover Richmond.
Flood frame: the district is on Lulu Isl: Flooding: the area is on Lulu Island in the Fraser River floodplain, behind the City's perimeter dikes and drainage pump stations, built for a 1-in-500-year flood, with dikes being raised from 3.5 to 4.7 metres. The Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels.
Where the condo stock concentrates: it d: Where the condos are: there aren't really any. The area is mostly detached houses in the RS1/RS2 zones under Zoning Bylaw 8500, and the newer named strata complexes are townhouses, not apartments.
Anchors: Garry Point Park, a 39-acre wat: Landmarks: Garry Point Park, a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park, on the old BC Packers cannery site; the West Dyke Trail; Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, a 30-acre park with the community centre, pool and library; the Steveston library branch (Easthope Hub), 4320 Moncton Street; and the Gulf of Georgia Cannery, 12138 4th Avenue, a national historic site.

Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels.

Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204 + St: Flooding and dikes: the Flood Plain Designation and Protection Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels. For lots on or near the water or dike, check both before pricing a rebuild or addition, and keep an eye on the City's Steveston Island Dike project, its long-term flood project for this waterfront.
Landmarks that frame the land: the Gulf: Landmarks: the Gulf of Georgia Cannery, 12138 4th Avenue, is a national historic site; Garry Point Park is a 39-acre waterfront park at the mouth of the Fraser; Imperial Landing Waterfront Park is on the old BC Packers cannery site; and Steveston Community Park, 4011 Moncton Street, is a 30-acre park with the community centre, pool and library.
Flood / dike diligence — Bylaw 8204: the: Flooding and dikes: the village is on the South Arm of the Fraser behind the City's dikes. Richmond is a low-lying city in the Fraser floodplain, protected by 49 km of dikes and 39 pump stations built for a 1-in-500-year flood, with dikes being raised from 3.5 to 4.7 metres, and Bylaw 8204 sets dike setbacks and flood construction levels. The City's Steveston Island Dike project, a proposed dike around Steveston Island from London Farm to Garry Point Park with a navigation gate for Steveston Harbour, would protect the waterfront and harbour. Check the lot's flood construction level and dike setback before planning a rebuild.
Schools: Westwind Elementary, K-7, SD38: Schools (SD38 Richmond): Westwind Elementary (K–7), 11371 Kingfisher Drive; R.A. McMath Secondary (8–12), 4251 Garry Street; and Hugh Boyd Secondary (8–12). Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
The one age-restricted strata ownership: The area's only age-restricted strata complex: gated freehold strata townhouses, built in 1992, 91 units, zoned RTL 1. A current listing calls it a "55+ gated townhouse community" and lists its restrictions as age restricted 55+, pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed with restrictions, and it's described as adult oriented, with a clubhouse and hot tub. It's in the Terra Nova area, despite the "Quilchena" name.
Recreation, library, health: Thompson Co: Recreation, library and health: Thompson Community Centre is at 5151 Granville Avenue in the wider Thompson area. There's no library branch here; the nearest is Brighouse (main), 100-7700 Minoru Gate. The nearest hospital is Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway, and the Richmond City Centre Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #110-4671 No. 3 Road.
The pocket's Indigenous and settler name: The area has both an Indigenous and a settler name in everyday use: Indigenous Peoples used Terra Nova for seasonal fishing camps during the salmon and sturgeon runs, and called it Spul'u'kwuks (now the elementary school's name) before Newfoundland fishermen renamed it Terra Nova, "new land". The Terra Nova Cannery was built here and ran until the mid-1900s.
One complex: Quilchena Green, 5531 Cornw: One complex: Quilchena Green, 5531 Cornwall Drive, 91 gated freehold strata townhouses built in 1992; the current listing says "Age Restricted 55+." It's the area's only age-restricted strata; the others here (Sonoma, Mayflower and London Mews) have no age limit.
A gated townhouse complex of duplex-styl: A gated complex of two-level, duplex-style townhomes: 91 homes, built in 1992, wood frame, freehold strata, Strata Plan LMS423, zoned RTL 1 according to a listing. A building directory mentions a clubhouse and hot tub, and listings describe a live-in caretaker. Sources differ on the rules: a current listing says age restricted 55+, pets allowed with restrictions (one cat or dog) and rentals allowed with restrictions, while the directory says rentals aren't allowed; long-term rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022 anyway.
A gated townhouse community built 1995 (: A gated townhouse community built in 1995, according to listings: freehold strata, wood frame, with an outdoor pool, hot tub, clubhouse, gym and landscaped grounds. Some listings call a unit a townhouse and others a duplex or half duplex, but it's one gated strata townhouse community.
Care anchors are in the wider Thompson /: Services are in the wider Thompson and City Centre area, not here. Thompson Community Centre is at 5151 Granville Avenue; the nearest hospital is Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway, and the Richmond City Centre Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at #110-4671 No. 3 Road. There's no library branch here; the nearest is Brighouse (main), 100-7700 Minoru Gate.
ALR vs non-ALR split: the pocket's house: ALR or not: the house lots here aren't in the ALR; the farmland to the west and south is ALR land, zoned AG1.
ALR rules (the farm-land framework): sub: ALR rules for the farmland: subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, homes can't be stratified, and each parcel can have one main house (up to 500 m², with a suite only inside it) plus, if the rules are met, one additional home of up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm tax status, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.
Strata block — applies to the built town: Strata rules (for the townhouse complexes such as Quilchena Green, not bare land): check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (a registered rental covenant is a separate matter), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children.
By Polygon. Current listings date the bu: Built by Polygon. Listings date the buildings to 2015 (Alexandra Road addresses) and 2016–2017 (Tomicki Avenue addresses), so the year depends on the address. A building directory lists a 136-unit wood-frame development at 9366 Tomicki Avenue and a 138-unit one at 9399 Alexandra Road. Listings mention geothermal heating and cooling (from the Alexandra District Energy Utility), air conditioning, 9-foot ceilings and a 12,000 sq ft clubhouse with an outdoor pool, hot tub, gym, basketball court and guest suites. Listings say pets are allowed (one says 2 pets, no size limit).
By Polygon, designed by Robert Ciccozzi: Built by Polygon and designed by Robert Ciccozzi, according to listings, in the Alexandra Gardens neighbourhood. Listings say 2011 and 2012 and a building directory says 2013, which fits a phased build. The directory says pets are allowed with restrictions (for 9388 McKim Way). Amenities include air conditioning, a clubhouse (the Mayfair Club, over 8,000 sq ft according to listings), elevator, garden, guest suite, outdoor pool and hot tub. Listings describe one building as wood frame with a brick and mixed exterior.
Serviced position — split, as the Area P: Services vary: the Area Plan said the Alexandra part of West Cambie was still on septic systems on its older lots, so check sewer servicing for an older Alexandra lot; any wells are listed in the provincial well registry (GWELLS).
Alexandra District Energy Utility (ADEU): Alexandra District Energy Utility: the City's list of connected apartment buildings includes buildings on Alexandra Road, Odlin Road and Tomicki Avenue (among them Alexandra Court, Mayfair Place, Omega and Trafalgar). Omega's Low End Market Rental (LEMR) uni: Omega's Low End Market Rental units (9333 Tomicki Avenue / 9388 Odlin Road) are affordable rental units inside a market strata building, secured by a registered housing covenant. They aren't for sale as market homes, and the covenant still applies even though strata rental bans were voided in 2022.
Main roads: Cambie Road, Garden City Roa: Main roads: Cambie Road, Garden City Road, Alderbridge Way, No. 4 Road and Westminster Highway, with Highway 91 to the east and Highway 99 to the west and south from the City Centre side; the Area Plan notes the City Centre is within walking distance. Civic anchors: Alexandra Park, 9600 Odli: Nearby: Alexandra Park, 9600 Odlin Road, linked by parts of the Alexandra Greenway between the Garden City Lands and Cambie Road; Garden City Community Park, 6620 Garden City Road, beside the area; Cambie Community Centre, 12800 Cambie Road, to the east; the Brighouse (main) library branch, 100-7700 Minoru Gate, and the Cambie branch, 150-11590 Cambie Road; and Richmond Hospital, 7000 Westminster Highway.

Schools: William Cook Elementary, grades: Schools (SD38 Richmond): William Cook Elementary (K–7), 8600 Cook Road; Samuel Brighouse Elementary (K–7), 6800 Azure Road; and Richmond Secondary (8–12), 7171 Minoru Boulevard. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.

Subdivision + servicing — verified for R: Subdivision and servicing: Richmond's Subdivision and Development Bylaw 8751 (2011) sets the subdivision and servicing rules, with costs recovered under the Works and Services Cost Recovery Bylaw 8752 (2011). SSMUH position — Richmond's own, as the: Small-scale housing in Richmond: the City allows at least one secondary suite or extra unit per lot, and the provincial small-scale housing rules allow at least 3 units on lots of 280 m² or less and 4 on larger lots, with a duplex as the basic form. A strata lot in a multi-unit strata plan: A strata lot in a multi-unit strata plan, not a two-lot strata or a fee-simple half. Read the whole Form B; it confirms the strata plan number and all the rules.

Flood — this sub-area's defining diligen: Flooding is the key check here: the City's floodplain study puts the Downtown waterfront in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront, where many newer buildings have their floors above the flood construction level but exits and the waterfront path are below it. The Royal Avenue slope complexes are above the waterfront, but the check is the same: confirm the building's flood construction level compliance, strata insurance and deductible before removing subjects. The City publishes flood information for its low-lying areas.

A current listing names the building Que: A current listing calls the building Queen's Park Place, built in 1994, and describes it as a quiet 55+ building. A 55+ bylaw is the only age bylaw allowed in BC; check the registered bylaw and its exemptions on the Form B.

Listings record Sub-Type Townhouse, buil: Listings show wood-frame townhouses built in 2007, with access to the shared Boiler House amenity centre (gym, theatre, half basketball court and lounge) and a clubhouse, gym, recreation facilities, grounds maintenance, management and snow removal. Five of the city's twelve square kilomet: Five of the city's 12 square kilometres are inside the flood boundaries: the City says Queensborough and parts of the mainland are in the provincial floodplain, but it doesn't give a zone number for Fraserview's residential slope (Zone 2 in its study is the commercial and industrial river land at the west end). Check the specific lot with the City rather than borrowing a zone from another area.

The Quay has two names and both are offi: The Quay goes by two names: the real estate board calls it "Quay", while the City's heritage documents use "Quayside", as do the street, park and bus route. Search under both names, or you'll miss listings under the other one.
Heritage Conservation Area — the definin: The Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area is the key rule here. It's New Westminster's only heritage conservation area, and it covers every property in the area, whatever its age, classed as Protected or Non-protected. Building permits for new buildings, demolition or changes to the front, sides or visible roofline of a Protected property, and subdivision applications, need a Heritage Alteration Permit, reviewed against design guidelines; Protected properties also need one for exterior changes that don't need a building permit. Protected properties must meet the Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw, though like-for-like maintenance doesn't need a permit. Protected properties get incentives: extra density, special Building Code provisions, density transfer, more flexible laneway and carriage house rules and no heritage permit fees. How the rules apply to a strata building's exterior common property is a question for the City; check for the specific building before pricing exterior work.
THE defining diligence item for this sub: The key check here is the heritage conservation area, not flooding. The Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area is New Westminster's only one, and every property in it is classed as Protected or Non-protected, whatever its age. Protected properties must meet the Heritage Property Maintenance Standards Bylaw, though like-for-like maintenance doesn't need a permit, and they get incentives: extra density, density transfer, special Building Code provisions, more flexible laneway and carriage house rules and no heritage permit fees. Clinton Place (built 1974) is inside the area, so exterior and common-property work may need a permit; check its Protected or Non-protected status and the strata's obligations with the City before pricing any exterior project.

Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680 (2001): t: Zoning (Bylaw 6680, 2001): Queensborough has its own rule: in District Lots 757 and 758, a subdivision can't create a lot under half an acre (0.20 ha) or with less than 66 feet (20.12 m) of frontage unless it can connect to City sewer. Across the city, the older townhouse zones are RT-2 to RT-2C plus RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B (the Jardine Street townhouse site above is RT-3). The newer RT-A and RT-B zones are part of the City's townhouse program, which its guide says applies on the mainland, not in Queensborough.
Floodplain diligence — THE defining item: Flooding is the key check in Queensborough: the City's floodplain study puts it in Floodplain Zone 1, a low-lying area with high groundwater, poor soft soils and poor drainage, protected by dikes and pumped drainage shared with Richmond, with the City as the diking authority. A perimeter dike built in the 1960s protects about 350 hectares; Queensborough has 350 hectares of designated floodplain and is the City's top priority for flood protection upgrades. Queensborough and parts of the mainland are in the provincial floodplain.
Strata diligence (island strata stock):: Strata rules: for a strata home on the island, look at the depreciation report and reserve fund early; strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal. For any strata lot, check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve, rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.
Brunette is the east-side New Westminste: Brunette is on New Westminster's east side, along the Brunette River corridor and Hume Park, right at the Coquitlam boundary. "Brunette" is the real estate board's name, not a City neighbourhood plan name; the City plans this edge through Our City 2041 (OCP Bylaw 7925, 2017) and the Sapperton/Braid Frequent Transit Development Area.
Amenity anchors: Hume Park and Lower Hum: Nearby: Hume Park and Lower Hume Park (outdoor pool, spray park, sports fields, lacrosse box and off-leash dog area) are in the area; Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, is the regional hospital at the Sapperton edge; and the main library is at 716 6th Avenue.
City zoning and plan — corrected distric: Zoning and plans: Zoning Bylaw 6680 (2001) and Our City 2041 (OCP Bylaw 7925, 2017). The townhouse zones are RT-2 to RT-2C, plus RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough; RT-2 allows 18 units per net acre (floor space ratio 0.6), a height of 25 feet and 40% site coverage. The house zone here, RS-1, sets a minimum lot of 557.4 m² (6,000 sq ft) and a floor space ratio of 0.5.
Suites as the City states them: one seco: Suites: one secondary suite per house, and the City allows a property to have both a secondary suite and a laneway or carriage house (the bylaw section other sources quote is 190.29; check the current bylaw text before relying on it). In multi-unit buildings, at least 40% of single-storey units must be adaptable (Adaptable Housing Bylaw 7464, 2011).
Floodplain — the corridor's defining dil: Flooding is the key check on this corridor: the City's floodplain study puts the industrial land along the Brunette River in Floodplain Zone 4, below the flood construction level, which matters for any land assembly, infill or insurance question here.
The sub-area's name crosses a city line: The name crosses a city line the area doesn't: Brunette Avenue and Brunette Creek run from New Westminster up into Coquitlam's Maillardville side, so "Brunette" searches mix two cities, two school districts and two sets of rules, and the only named townhouse complex that comes up (Brunette Villas) is on the Coquitlam side.
A 0/0 market row is itself the market fa: In September 2026, Brunette had nothing listed or sold, detached or attached. Any "Brunette townhouse" listing should be checked first for which side of the city boundary it's on.
Industrial corridor land: the City's flo: Industrial land: the City's floodplain study mentions industrial land along the Brunette River here, so this is a mix of homes, creek corridor and industrial edge, not a uniform residential neighbourhood. That industrial land is floodplain, not land for sale.
Serviced position, as the City states it: Services: New Westminster runs its own electrical utility as well as City water and sewer. Servicing for a specific lot is settled through the City's subdivision process under Bylaw 7142 (2007).
No named bare-land development, assembly: I don't know of any land development, assembly, development site or rezoning in Brunette. Growth here is planned through the Sapperton/Braid Frequent Transit Development Area in Our City 2041, a City designation, not land for sale.
Market context: September 2026 SnapStats: Market figures, September 2026: Brunette had no detached homes, condos or townhomes listed or sold. New Westminster's medians were $1,365,000 for detached homes and $560,000 for condos and townhomes.

No condo building or townhome complex na: I don't know of any condo building or townhouse complex in Brunette, and none were for sale in September 2026. If you want this corridor, you're buying a detached house, or looking in Sapperton.
Houses are effectively the whole stock h: Houses are basically everything here: detached houses in the Single Detached Residential (RS) zones of Zoning Bylaw 6680, with secondary suites and laneway or carriage house potential under the same bylaw. Sapperton Green — 97 Braid Street, aroun: Sapperton Green, 97 Braid Street, around Braid Station: the 38.35-acre former industrial site is designated in the OCP as the Sapperton Green Transit-Oriented Mixed-Use Community. The master plan concept endorsed by Council (a QuadReal Property Group application) proposes about 4,700 homes (including at least 1,122,000 sq ft of secured market rental and at least 255,000 sq ft of affordable housing under the City's Inclusionary Housing Policy), 750,000 to 1.5 million sq ft of office space, 100,000 to 150,000 sq ft of retail, a 35,000 sq ft community centre with child care, and 7.9 acres of public open space, with a planned connection to the Sapperton District Energy System. It's the area's one big land story, but it's a plan, not a presale or land for sale; sellers may mention it, but buyers shouldn't pay today for amenities that aren't built.
Sapperton is the historic neighbourhood: Sapperton is the historic neighbourhood at New Westminster's northeast end, on the slope above the Fraser between McBride Boulevard and the Coquitlam boundary at Brunette Creek, including Royal Columbian Hospital, Sapperton and Braid SkyTrain stations, Hume Park and the Brewery District. The City also calls it "McBride-Sapperton", and "Sapperton" is the real estate board's name. The name comes from the Royal Engineers' 1858 camp, nicknamed "Sappers' Town" after the Sapper rank, and it stuck after the corps disbanded.

A 75-unit, 16-storey mixed-use high-rise: A 75-unit, 16-storey mixed-use tower by Tridecca, completed in 2014, with shops on the ground floor; listings show freehold strata condos in Uptown.

Check a specific lot with the City.
Form B diligence (any Uptown strata, inc: For any Uptown strata, including Penny Lane, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. OCP \"Our City 2041,\" Bylaw No. 7925, 2: Plans and zoning: under Our City 2041 (OCP Bylaw 7925, 2017), Uptown is a Frequent Transit Development Area, with higher-density growth aimed at the Sixth Street and Sixth Avenue core (a planning direction, not a rezoning of any lot). RS-1 sets a minimum lot of 557.4 m² and a floor space ratio of 0.5; secondary suites are allowed in the RS zones, and the same bylaw covers laneway and carriage houses. The Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area is just east; Uptown is outside it, so heritage status depends on the property.
Its listings split: one unit is filed Ap: Listings for this one differ: one unit is listed as an apartment, another as a townhouse. It's shown once, with the condos. It's a strata low-rise, so check the unit's form on the strata plan and Form B.
The residential side streets off the Six: The side streets off the Sixth Street core are detached homes in the Single Detached Residential (RS) zones of Zoning Bylaw 6680, a mix of the city's older houses and later infill. RS-1 sets a minimum lot of 557.4 m² (6,000 sq ft) and a floor space ratio of 0.5. Most side-street homes are freehold: a fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees; the title, City bylaws and any registered covenants apply.
City plans and zoning (New Westminster's: Plans and zoning: Our City 2041 (OCP Bylaw 7925, 2017) and Zoning Bylaw 6680 (2001). The apartment buildings are along the Sixth Street and Sixth Avenue core, in the multi-family and high-rise commercial zones, while the side streets are in the RS zones (RS-1: minimum lot 557.4 m², or 6,000 sq ft, and a floor space ratio of 0.5). Secondary suites are allowed in the RS zones, and the same bylaw covers laneway and carriage houses.
Schools: Fraser River Middle, 6–8, 800 Q: Schools (SD40 New Westminster): Lord Kelvin Elementary (K–5), 1010 Hamilton Street; Fraser River Middle (6–8), 800 Queens Avenue; and New Westminster Secondary (9–12), 820 6th Street. Check the catchment for a specific address with the school district.
Lower Twelfth Street land assembly, City: Lower Twelfth Street land assembly: the City bought three properties (235 Thirteenth Street, 240 Twelfth Street and 221 Twelfth Street), taking possession on September 15, 2026, for $28.5 million in total from City reserves. Subdividing land in the ALR requires the: Subdividing ALR land needs the Agricultural Land Commission's approval, and registering a strata plan counts as subdividing, so homes on ALR land can't be stratified without the Commission's permission. It's a permission rule, not an outright ban, but price an ALR parcel as one parcel unless that permission exists. A bare-land strata lot is strata ownership, with a Form B, fees and bylaws, which is the opposite of buying a fee-simple acreage.
Since November 24, 2022 for strata prope: Since November 24, 2022, strata bylaws anywhere in BC can't ban or limit long-term rentals, so a "rentals not allowed" line in a listing or building directory doesn't apply to long-term rentals. Short-term rentals are different: stratas can still ban or limit them by bylaw, local zoning may restrict them, and a provincial short-term rental registration number has been required since May 1, 2025. Age bylaws: only a 55-and-older bylaw is allowed, with exemptions for existing residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses or partners and some children.
Strata Property Act s. 59 — states the l: The Form B shows a strata lot's monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. The strata paperwork is where a strata home's real cost shows up: the Province's guidance points buyers to the Form B, the Form F, the bylaws and rules, fees and special levies, and that's where age, pet and rental rules are, not in the listing.
Published lines: Eight West — pets allow: Pet bylaws can still be enforced in BC, unlike rental bans, so check the registered bylaws in the Form B package for the specific building. Listing lines such as "pets allowed" or "cats OK" aren't the bylaws.
1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,0: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million and 3% above $2 million, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. The newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and ends at $1,150,000; it's for new homes, not bare land. Examples (fully residential, no exemption): $500,000 → $8,000; $700,000 → $12,000; $800,000 → $14,000 (a qualifying first-time buyer pays $6,000); $900,000 → $16,000; $1,000,000 → $18,000; $1,200,000 → $22,000; $1,500,000 → $28,000; $1,800,000 → $34,000; $2,000,000 → $38,000; and $3,500,000 → $93,000, including the extra 2% ($10,000) on the $500,000 over $3 million.
By zone: RS Large Lot Residential carrie: It depends on the zone: each city's zoning bylaw sets the minimum size for a new lot, and that minimum applies when you subdivide, not when you build on an existing lot. Check the parcel's zone with the city or regional district.
since July 1, 2024, strata corporations: Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get a depreciation report every five years and can't vote to skip it. Since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go into the contingency reserve fund. Since November 24, 2022, strata bylaws can't ban or limit long-term rentals (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older; it applies to who lives there, not who owns.
PTT is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from: Property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million and 3% above $2 million, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million. For example, an $800,000 townhouse with no exemption pays $14,000 ($2,000 + $12,000), and a $600,000 townhouse pays $10,000, or $2,000 for a qualifying first-time buyer (exempt on the first $500,000). The first-time buyers' GST rebate (law since March 13, 2026) covers all the GST up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out at $1.5 million, for agreements from March 20, 2025 to 2031; the GST New Housing Rebate is 36% up to $6,300 (phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000); the Home Buyers' Plan allows $60,000, an FHSA $8,000 a year up to $40,000, and CMHC premiums run 0.6%–4.5%. 5% GST applies to new homes (developer sales and presales), not resales.
A buyer of a strata townhouse is entitle: When you're buying a strata townhouse, you're entitled to a Form B (Information Certificate) within seven days of asking, for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page for paper copies. It shows the monthly strata fee, anything the owner owes the strata, special levies approved but not yet due, the contingency reserve balance, the strata's insurance, its rules, budget and financial statement, any rental disclosure statement, and the current depreciation report.
general rates 1% of fair market value up: General rates: 1% of fair market value up to $200,000, 2% on the part from $200,000 to $2,000,000, and 3% on the part above $2,000,000. Examples: $700,000 → $12,000; $1,000,000 → $18,000; $1,200,000 → $22,000; $1,500,000 → $28,000. The newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000, phases out over the next $50,000 and ends at $1,150,000.
Only 55+ age bylaws are valid since Nove: Since November 24, 2022, only 55-and-older age bylaws are valid, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers and existing residents (expanded on May 1, 2023); a 45+ bylaw is void and doesn't turn into a 55+ one.
Municipal layer: an Abbotsford-ground pa: City rules: a parcel in Abbotsford falls under Abbotsforward 2050, the OCP adopted in December 2025 (older plan numbers like 2600-2016 are out of date), and Zoning Bylaw 2400 (2014). Each parcel follows its own city's rules; check with that city.
Subdivision of ALR land generally requir: Subdividing ALR land generally needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and registering a strata plan counts as subdividing. It's a permission rule, not an outright ban, but never assume you'll get it.
Where the condo stock actually concentra: Where the condos are: not in Calverhall. I don't know of any condo or townhouse complex in the area.

Mission / FVRD frames (each as its own):: Mission and the regional district each have their own rules. City of Mission: OCP Bylaw 6405-2026 (adopted June 1, 2026), Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020, small-scale housing Bylaw 6299-2024 and development servicing Bylaw 5650-2017, with a flat 10% tax penalty after July 2 and no Supreme Court registry. Rural Fraser Valley Regional District land: taxes are due July 2, with 5% added on amounts unpaid then and another 5% on amounts unpaid October 31, billed by the Surveyor of Taxes and paid to the Province. Which rules apply depends on the parcel's jurisdiction, not its mailing address or real estate board area.
There is no acreage statistic to hide be: There's no market figure for acreages: every city figure you see next to an acreage listing is a housing figure (detached, or condos and townhomes combined) that includes acreages without measuring them. Price an acreage parcel by parcel, using its own area's sales, its ALR status, water, buildings and farm income; it's the only reliable way.
The stratification sentence is the valle: The rule people most often get wrong: ALR land "cannot be stratified without the Agricultural Land Commission's permission". It's a permission rule, not an outright ban.

Own-land manufactured-home stock is a di: Owning the land is different: in a bare-land strata park you own your lot as a strata lot, with a Form B, strata fees and registered bylaws, and no pad rent. In a co-op, the co-op holds the land and you hold a co-op share plus the home. On fee-simple land you own the parcel outright.
Yes, as a park designation under the pro: Yes, as a park designation: the Province says that in a designated 55-plus park, at least one tenant on the site must be 55 or older. That's a different legal rule from a strata's 55+ bylaw, so strata exemptions don't apply to a pad tenancy; read the park's tenancy agreement and rules, which can be stricter.
Where the housing stock is: only Burkevi: Homes: only in Burkeville, a pocket of detached houses built for aviation workers in three designs; the City of Richmond Archives says Burkeville is the only community left on Sea Island. There are no townhouses.
Why this section exists on a zero-stock: There are no strata homes on Sea Island today. For any strata property, review the strata documents; strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal.
Form B diligence (any future strata purc: For any strata purchase, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.
The everyday anchors are small and speci: Everyday places are few: Burkeville Park and the Sea Island Community Centre at 7140 Miller Road; Larry Berg Flight Path Park on Russ Baker Way; McDonald Beach Park at the end of McDonald Road; Iona Beach Regional Park at 900 Ferguson Road, at the island's northwest end; and the Sea Island Conservation Area, a protected habitat.
Housing on Sea Island exists only in Bur: The only homes on Sea Island are in Burkeville, a pocket of detached houses on the southeast part of the island, built for aviation workers in three designs; the City of Richmond Archives says Burkeville is the only community left on Sea Island. They're existing houses, not land for sale.
ALR vs non-ALR: Sea Island was once most: ALR or not: Sea Island was once mostly farmland with small communities including Eburne and Burkeville, according to the City Archives, but that's history. I don't know of any current ALR land on Sea Island; check a specific parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission's map.
Because the only permitted stats source: Because the market report I use doesn't publish one: it reports condos and townhomes together, with medians only at the city level.
subdivision parcel area, shape and dimen: A new lot's area, shape and dimensions must meet the zoning for its zone, and the city can require roads and lanes, water, sewer and drainage connected to its systems, built to its engineering standards. Each city has its own subdivision and servicing bylaw (Burnaby's, for example, was updated in 2024, with a guide for four or more homes on a residential lot). Check the requirements for a specific parcel with the city's engineering department before pricing a lot split.
1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,0: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million and 3% above $2 million, plus another 2% on the residential part above $3 million; a purchase under $2 million pays only the 1% and 2% rates. The newly built home exemption is full up to $1,100,000 and partial up to $1,150,000.
since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or: Since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must get one every five years and can't vote to skip it, and since November 1, 2023, at least 10% of the operating budget must go into the contingency reserve. An older building with a pool, hot tub or recreation centre carries roof, building envelope and amenity costs that show up in its fees, so read the depreciation report before comparing its fees with a newer or simpler building's.
Home Buyers' Plan $60,000 per buyer from: Home Buyers' Plan: $60,000 per buyer from RRSPs. First Home Savings Account: $8,000 a year, up to $40,000. Mortgage default insurance (CMHC): premiums run 0.6% to 4.5%, plus 0.2% where the over-25-year amortization surcharge applies.
published premiums run 0.60% (LTV up to: Premiums run from 0.6% (borrowing up to 65% of the price) to 4.0% (90.01% to 95%), or 4.5% at the top with a non-traditional down payment, plus 0.2% where the over-25-year amortization surcharge applies.
The strata package behind the Form B: th: The strata package behind the Form B: the depreciation report (required every five years for stratas with 5 or more lots since July 1, 2024), financial statements, the contingency reserve balance and planned work, which BCREA advises reviewing to spot future special levies. In an older building, that package matters more than the staging.
a presale buyer must receive the develop: A presale buyer must get the developer's disclosure statement, deposits are held in trust, and the buyer can cancel within 7 days of the later of signing the contract or receiving the disclosure statement. This applies to any townhouse bought from a developer.
Short-term rentals are prohibited in Pit: Cities can ban short-term rentals in their zoning even though strata rental bans are void; Pitt Meadows, for example, doesn't allow short-term rental accommodation in its zoning bylaw. Don't price a townhouse on short-term rental income without checking the city's rules.
Rental-restriction bylaws void since Nov: Strata rental bans have been void since November 24, 2022, but short-term rentals can still be restricted by strata bylaw, and many cities license them separately (Chilliwack, for example, under its Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141). Check that a property can be licensed before counting on short-term rental income.

R-CL compact lots (Zoning Bylaw No. 2500: Compact lots (R-CL): the Residential Compact Lot zone is Willoughby's small-lot pattern, covering both front-loaded lots and rear-loaded lots with lane access. In the City of Langley, land designated: In the City of Langley, land designated Mid Rise Residential needs a development permit for the building's form and character, which shapes the new apartment buildings going up here. The Official Community Plan (OCP) sorts: The Official Community Plan sorts homes by type: high-density mixed-use in the "Core" around the planned SkyTrain stations near 196 Street and 203 Street, mid-rises up to 12 storeys, low-rises up to 6 storeys, townhouses along future frequent bus routes, and compact lots with secondary or garden suites north of Grade Crescent.
No — separate municipalities, separate b: No. They're separate municipalities with separate bylaws. In the City: Zoning Bylaw 3300 (2025) and small-scale housing Bylaw 3284 apply, and a suite can be 100 m² or 40% of the home, whichever is less, with the owner living there. A park's 55+ rule has its own legal foot: A park's 55+ rule has its own legal basis: BC's manufactured home park rules recognize parks where every pad is reserved for someone 55 or older (or two or more people, at least one of them 55 or older), and the park owner can refuse a sale where no buyer meets that age. That's how the 55+ rules at the three Newton and Fleetwood parks work; I don't know of any pad-rental park in South Surrey.
Assignment consent has a clock: Under MH: Consent has a deadline: a seller can assign the pad tenancy only with the landlord's written consent first (or deemed consent), an arbitrator's order, or where the tenancy agreement allows it. The park owner must answer within 10 days of the written request (RTB Form 10), silence counts as consent, and no fee can be charged. Before asking, the seller must give the buyer written copies of the park rules and the relevant parts of the tenancy agreement.
Park closure / conversion (MHPTA s. 42,: Park closure or conversion: if a landlord plans to convert all or much of a park to another use, they must have all the government permits and approvals first, give 12 months' notice, and pay each tenant $20,000 by the date the notice takes effect. The tenant can move out early with at least 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can apply for more compensation (the home's assessed value minus the $20,000). Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw (2025) doesn't apply to manufactured home parks.

A transfer does not trigger a market re-: A sale doesn't reset the pad rent to market. Unlike a strata, where fees follow the current budget, an assignment passes the current pad rent and the date of the next increase to the buyer. The rent history is in the tenancy agreement, which the seller must share before asking the park for consent.
\"55+\" in a Langley park and \"55+\" in: "55+" in a Langley park and "55+" in a Langley strata are legally different. A park's rule is in the tenancy regulation and park rules and can be a reason to refuse a sale; a strata's rule is a registered bylaw with set exemptions. A couple who can live in a Parkway Estates strata unit on a spouse exemption don't automatically have the same right in a Brookswood park.
Under MHPTA s. 42: the landlord must fir: If a park is being closed or converted, the landlord must have all the permits and approvals first, then give 12 months' notice and pay each tenant $20,000 by the date the notice takes effect. The tenant can leave early with 10 days' written notice, can dispute the notice within 15 days, and in some cases can claim more (the home's assessed value minus the $20,000). If the landlord doesn't go ahead within a reasonable time, they owe a further $5,000 or 12 months' rent, whichever is more.
